title: New US air weapon sparks UFO theories: Lockheed Martin unveils Vectis combat drone
excerpt: New US air weapon sparks UFO theories: Lockheed Martin unveils Vectis combat drone
content:
mystery

Express newspaper

15/09/2026 13:56

One of the world's largest defense and aerospace technology companies has publicly unveiled a full-scale model of a new combat drone, immediately sparking a wave of online theories that its technology may be related to UFOs.

Lockheed Martin has unveiled the full-scale model of the Vectis , an autonomous unmanned combat aircraft developed by its secretive Skunk Works division. The program was first announced in 2025, and the company has now shown the full-scale model for the first time and confirmed that it is expanding production of experimental vehicles.

Vectis is designed to fly independently or operate alongside manned aircraft, such as the F-35, performing combat, reconnaissance and support missions. Lockheed Martin aims to have the first prototype flying by the end of 2027.

A mysterious message sparked speculation

Ahead of the public launch, Skunk Works posted the silhouette of an unknown aircraft on social media, along with a mysterious message suggesting that the "next level has been unlocked."

The futuristic look was enough for some social media users to revive old theories according to which American defense companies may have developed technology by studying crashed extraterrestrial vehicles.

"Okay, now show us the tools you rebuilt," one user wrote.

Another commented: "Now show us the anti-gravity planes you've hidden from the public for 70 years."

No verifiable evidence has been presented for such claims.

The Pentagon and the US government have repeatedly stated that the existence of physical evidence proving the recovery of vehicles of extraterrestrial origin has not been confirmed.

What can Vectis do?

According to Lockheed Martin, Vectis is designed as a multi-role autonomous combat aircraft, capable of cooperating with manned aircraft and next-generation platforms.

The company says its architecture is built so that the system can be continuously improved and adapted to the mission.

Lockheed describes Vectis as a platform that aims to bring new levels of combat survivability, operational flexibility and strike capabilities to the US and its allies.

The program envisages the construction of four more vehicles, in addition to the initial prototype, while the first flight remains planned for 2027.

Design built to evade radars

The Vectis has a futuristic tailless shape, with a "flying wing" configuration, a design that helps reduce radar signature and aerodynamic drag.

The engine is integrated in order to reduce exposure to adversary sensors.

Lockheed Martin has also confirmed that the prototype will use the Williams International FJ44-4 turbofan engine , which produces over 3,600 pounds of thrust and was chosen due to its reliability and ability to accelerate the testing program.

The aircraft will be able to carry weapons inside the fuselage, an important feature for maintaining stealth capabilities.

UFO theories bring back an old story

The speculation that accompanied the presentation is not new for Lockheed Martin.

One of the most prominent former employees to claim links between the company and UFOs was Boyd Bushman, a former Lockheed Martin and Texas Instruments engineer who died in 2014.

Before his death, Bushman claimed to have worked on secret projects linking UFOs and extraterrestrial beings with attempts to reconstruct their technology.

He even published photographs that he claimed showed extraterrestrial beings linked to projects at Area 51.

Bushman's claims have never been verified. Skeptics have argued that the figures in some of the photographs resembled dolls or props that could be purchased commercially.

Lockheed avoids comment on UFOs

Lockheed Martin has historically commented very little on theories linking its secret programs to materials of extraterrestrial origin.

When the company has previously been asked about unidentified aerial phenomena, now often called UAPs , it has directed questions towards the US government.

Skunk Works, founded in 1943, has a long history of secretly developing experimental and military aircraft.

Lockheed Martin has produced some of the most popular American aircraft, including the F-35, F-22 Raptor, and the C-130 transport aircraft.

It is precisely this history of secrecy and advanced technology that has helped fuel conspiracy theories over the years.

“Show us the other technology too”

Even after the introduction of Vectis, some users continued to claim that the company was hiding much more advanced technologies.

"Publish the tools reproduced from extraterrestrial technology. We know you produce them," wrote one user on X.

"It looks quite alien in design," commented another.

However, the futuristic appearance of an aircraft is not proof that its technology is of extraterrestrial origin.

Allegations of a secret American program

The debate over UFOs in the US has intensified in recent years due to statements by several former officials and whistleblowers.

Former Air Force officer David Grusch has publicly claimed that the US government had a secret program for recovering and analyzing objects of non-human origin.

Former CIA scientist Hal Puthoff has also made claims about secret programs linked to UAPs.

These claims have received considerable public and political attention, but the most extraordinary claims – including the existence of recovered extraterrestrial craft – have not yet been supported by verifiable, publicly available physical evidence.

The first prototype is expected to fly in 2027.

What is confirmed is that Vectis is a real and active Lockheed Martin program.

The model on display is life-size, while the company says it is continuing to build the functional prototype and four other vehicles.

The goal is for Vectis to make its first flight by the end of 2027 and then demonstrate the ability to cooperate with aircraft like the F-35 in future operations.

So while Vectis may seem like it came out of a science fiction movie, so far there is only evidence of an advanced American autonomous aircraft program – not technology taken from UFOs. /GazetaExpress/
